newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sees inflation slowing down in May.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sees inflation slowing down in May.

text.p: Philippine inflation is expected to slow down further in May from 4.6 percent in April, officials of the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) said on Thursday.
"It's decelerating. I'm quite confident that it will be lower," NEDA deputy director-general Dante Canlas told Reuters.
However, he said he did not expect the inflation to go below 4.4 percent, which is the lowest rate the government has projected for this year. It was attained last February.
The government lowered its average inflation projection for the whole year to be between 5.2 to 5.7 percent from 6.0 to 6.5 percent.
"We don't expect any price shock. We don't expect to see any of those blips in the foreseeable future," NEDA director-general Cielito Habito told reporters.
The April inflation dipped to 4.6 percent from 4.8 percent in March.
